Well... let me think about that. Actually, yes, there was this one specific stretch. It was maybe for a few weeks, and I remember it distinctly because we were in the middle of a major vendor integration project at work, which is usually a massive headache. But for whatever reason, during those several weeks, the heavy feeling... it just wasn't quite as heavy. It was like the pressure in my chest had let up just enough for me to take a full breath. I was actually getting through my work more normally, which was a huge relief. I was running my operations metrics, clearing out my inbox, and I wasn't having to stare blankly at my spreadsheets for an hour before I could type a single number. I really thought, oh my god, maybe this is it, maybe the cloud is finally moving on and I'm going to be okay again. 

But... the thing is, I wouldn't exactly say I felt like my old self. Because even though the sadness had backed off a bit and I had more energy, all the other stuff was still happening. It didn't go away at all. Like, I was still hearing that voice. The one that comes from near the air vents? I have this central heating vent right by the baseboards in my living room, the metal kind with the little slats, and there's another one right above my cubicle at the office, and the voice was still there. Just murmuring, right at the edge of my hearing. 

And on top of that, I was still completely convinced that I was being watched. I mean, I knew for a fact that the mortgage company was monitoring me. I kept going over it in my head, figuring out how they were tracking my property and my finances, just waiting for me to make one wrong move so they could swoop in. And it wasn't just them, it was my coworkers, too. Even though I was getting my work done and being productive, I couldn't shake the absolute certainty that they were keeping tabs on me. I'd look over and just know they were watching my screens, tracking my keystrokes, and reporting back on my every move. So, I was functioning better, and I wasn't crying all the time, but I was still living with this constant, exhausting reality of being monitored and hearing the vents. So... yeah, the mood lifted for a few weeks, but the rest of the nightmare just kept right on going.
